title: Stand With the Boycott?
summary: PLACEHOLDER CONTENT, not yet verified. Your town must decide whether to enforce a boycott of British goods.

briefing.heading: Welcome to 1775
briefing.text: Tension between Britain and its American colonies is rising. After the Boston Tea Party, Parliament closed Boston's port. Many colonists are angry.

briefing.heading: A boycott
briefing.text: Colonial leaders agreed to stop buying British goods. Now each town has to decide how seriously to enforce it. That is where you come in.

figures.name: Mr. Hale
figures.role: A local merchant who sells imported goods

figures.name: Mrs. Porter
figures.role: A member of the town's enforcement committee

merchant_intro.text: If I stop selling British cloth and tea, my family could lose everything. But my neighbors may stop trusting me if I keep selling.

choices.text: What happens if you keep selling?

merchant_risk.text: TODO: Peabody team writes what could happen to merchants who broke the boycott.

merchant_loyalty.text: TODO: Peabody team writes the merchant's mixed feelings.

committee_intro.text: Our committee watches who buys and sells British goods. If we are not united, Parliament will never listen.

choices.text: Is that fair to merchants like Mr. Hale?

committee_fair.text: TODO: Peabody team writes the committee member's response.

decision.prompt: The town meeting is tonight. What do you vote for?
decision.context: You do not know if Britain will back down, go to war, or punish towns that resist.

options.text: Allow merchants to sell what they already have
